Subject: Unexpected spike on May invoice — ratecard smoothing?

Hi Neha,

We're reviewing May's invoice and noticed a 14% jump in the line item labeled 'ratecard smoothing adjustment' compared to April. This doesn't line up with our usage patterns — total tokens were steady. Can you help explain what triggered the smoothing charge and whether it can be credited?

I've attached our internal usage extract for the month. If needed we can jump on a quick call later today.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform — Widgetly Inc.

Date: 2027-05-30T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected spike on May invoice — ratecard smoothing?

Ben / Connor — forwarding Widgetly's note. External says usage was steady but they were billed a smoothing adjustment of ~14% on May. I don't have the ratecard change details offhand. Can you triage?

Asks:
- Quick root cause: did a smoothing/rebalancing job reclassify a batch of requests into a higher tier?
- If so, what's the candidate credit and timeline to fix the invoice?

Marissa, adding you since this may need a proforma credit or invoice adjustment.

Thanks,
Neha
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected spike on May invoice — ratecard smoothing?

Quick update from engineering/ops: we rolled a smoothing patch on May 14 that changes how short-lived batched requests are bucketed across rate tiers when prefix caching misses occur. In most customers it reduced noise, but I can see an edge case where small, highly parallel batches that used to be amortized across lower tiers got reclassified into a higher effective rate for a small percentage of calls.

I ran a quick sample against Widgetly's attached CSV and reproduced a +/- 2.8% token increase in higher-tier classification for the affected time window (May 14–18). That's consistent with a one-off mis-bucketing during rollout.

Proposed remediation:
- Offer a one-time credit equal to 100% of the incremental higher-tier cost for May (estimate attached).
- Reprocess the affected window to produce a corrected usage export for Widgetly if they want full audit evidence.

I'm attaching a proposed credit calculation (proposed_credit_calc.xlsx) and the internal patch notes (redwood_ratecard_changes_May2027.pdf). If Widgetly signs off we'll issue a credit and update the May invoice.

Ben
Senior Account Engineer
attachments: proposed_credit_calc.xlsx, redwood_ratecard_changes_May2027.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@widgetly.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-31T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on May invoice — proposed credit and next steps

Hi Alex — thanks for flagging and for sending the usage extract.

We agree with Ben's assessment: an internal smoothing rollout changed classification for a narrow window and that produced an incremental higher-tier charge. We want to make this right.

What we propose: 
- Apply a one-time credit of $1,842.50 to the May invoice (this is 100% of the incremental higher-tier cost; breakdown attached).
- We will issue an updated invoice with the credit applied by Friday, June 4.
- If you prefer a reprocessed usage export for your records we can provide that within 3 business days.

Please reply with: 
1) Confirmation that the credit amount is acceptable, and
2) Whether you want the reprocessed export.

Once we have confirmation we'll queue the credit and deliver the corrected invoice.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed_credit_calc.xlsx
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@widgetly.ai>

Date: 2027-06-01T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on May invoice — proposed credit and next steps

Marissa / Neha — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear remediation plan.

We accept the $1,842.50 credit and would like the reprocessed usage export for our records. Please apply the credit to the May invoice and send the corrected PDF and the export when ready. If you can include a short note on the final invoice referencing RDW-2027-05-SMOOTH so our accounts payable team can match it, that would help.

Appreciate the quick response — happy to hop on a call if you need anything else.

Alex
Head of Platform, Widgetly Inc.
